I want to be fully transparent with you about what my research has found — and what it hasn't.

---

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Title** | *Molecular Biology of the Cell*, 7th Edition |
| **Authors** | Bruce Alberts, Rebecca Heald, Alexander Johnson, David Morgan, Martin Raff, Keith Roberts, Peter Walter |
| **Publisher** | W. W. Norton & Company |
| **Year** | 2022 |
| **ISBN** | 978-0-393-88423-5 (one variant listed) |

## What I Was Unable to Retrieve

Despite multiple searches and attempts to fetch the publisher's page, Wikipedia's chapter list, and other sources, **I was not able to retrieve a verified, chapter-by-chapter table of contents** for the 7th edition. The pages either returned only high-level summaries or could not be accessed. I won't fabricate a chapter list, as that could mislead your syllabus planning.

2. **Google Books preview:**
Search "Molecular Biology of the Cell 7th edition" on [books.google.com](https://books.google.com) — previews often include the table of contents pages.

Go to [wwnorton.com](https://wwnorton.com) and search for the book, or contact their academic sales/representative team directly. They often provide desk copies to instructors on request.

2. **Google Books preview** — Search the ISBN `978-0-393-88423-5` on [books.google.com](https://books.google.com). The TOC and some chapter previews are frequently accessible without purchase.

3. **Your library's copy or e-book access** — If your institution licenses the ebook through a platform like VitalSource, Chegg, or RedShelf, the full text including chapter summaries and section headings will be there.

4. **Request an instructor examination copy** — As a graduate course instructor, you are entitled to request a free exam copy directly from W. W. Norton. This is the gold standard for syllabus planning.
